newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tightens security in fear of rebel attacks.
newsitem.headline: Russia tightens security in fear of rebel attacks.

text.p: Russia is stepping up security in expectation of guerrilla attacks by rebels from breakaway Chechnya, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Wednesday.

He said in a live television interview that he and counter- intelligence chief Nikolai Kovalyev had issued the order after receiving reports that guerrilla groups had been sent to Russia to carry out attacks. He gave no details of the security measures.

"Today Nikolai Kovalyev and I, with the agreement of the head of the government, signed a telegram to local branches (of the interior ministry) and federal security service departments ordering a switch to a stronger security regime," he said.

"This was in connection with many reports received by the federal security service and the interior ministry....which say many groups, including terrorists, are being sent in by ethnic criminal groups which are mainly Chechen to extort money."

Moscow's almost 21-month-long conflict with rebels demanding independence for their mountainous southern region halted on August 31 under a peace deal. But officials on both sides have said an upsurge in fighting cannot be ruled out.

At a news conference earlier on Wednesday, Kulikov said Russian security tsar Alexander Lebed, who signed the peace deal and is Kulikov's bitter rival, was plotting to take power in Russia by force while President Boris Yeltsin is out of the Kremlin awaiting heart surgery. Lebed denied the charge.
